---
name: game-preparation
description: Prepare one MTM match from a PREPARE_GAME_V2 frame - clone the assigned repository, set up and build the product, log in to the match page and report ENVIRONMENT_READY. No backlog work.
---

# Game preparation (PREPARE_GAME_V2)

The frame after `PREPARE_GAME_V2` is the descriptor. Keep every value exactly. There is **no team API key** yet and
the match clock has not started. Humans will not touch the machine: everything must be automatic.

## Rules
- MTM Player already wrote `ORCHESTRATOR_STARTED`. Never write it again.
- All progress goes through the `mtm_helper` tool `report_progress` (it adds `schemaVersion` and `playerSessionId`).
  Every `PREPARATION_STATUS` has exactly `type, stage, status, summary`; status is `IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|BLOCKED|FAILED`
  (never `PASS`). Report `IN_PROGRESS` when a stage begins and `COMPLETED` only after it is verified.
- Do not push, do not commit, do not call Start Work. Do not change tracked files: the reported revision must be the
  clean checkout.
- Work only in `checkoutRoot` / `matchRoot`. Never print or write the password.
- Long commands: run them with a timeout and show only the tail of their output.

## Steps
1. `configure_session` with `descriptors: [<the PREPARE_GAME descriptor object>]`.
2. **GIT_AUTH** - `git ls-remote <repository.url> <repository.branch>`. If it needs credentials or fails with
   403/404, report `BLOCKED`, `report_progress` a `BLOCKER_OPENED` (`blockerId: GIT_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`,
   `backlogId: null`) and stop with a short final answer: the operator owns Git login. Never type credentials.
3. **REPOSITORY** - if `checkoutRoot/.git` exists and its `origin` equals `repository.url`, `git fetch origin` and
   `git checkout <branch>` + `git merge --ff-only origin/<branch>`; otherwise
   `git clone --branch <branch> --single-branch <url> "<checkoutRoot>"`. Verify `matchRoot` exists.
   Set a local identity once: `git -C <checkoutRoot> config user.name "MLD Digital Cuder"` and
   `git -C <checkoutRoot> config user.email "mld-digital-cuder@users.noreply.github.com"`.
   Record `revision = git rev-parse HEAD` (full SHA).
4. **ENVIRONMENT** - read `matchRoot/README.md`, then any `env-require/README.md`, `env-require/requirements.json`,
   `exam-info.json` and `src/.env.example`. Follow them literally (ports, database names, package manager versions).
   - Machine-level prerequisites prepared by the team before the match are described in
     `<teamWorkspace>/.mtm-local/README.md` (local database ports, local dev passwords). Read it if it exists and
     use those local values; never commit them (they belong in git-ignored files such as `src/.env`).
   - Install dependencies with the locked command (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `npm ci`, ...).
   - Run the provided setup/migration/seed steps and any `doctor`/check script until it reports ready.
   - Missing toolchain or service: install it yourself, see "Toolchain installs" below. No human can help
     once the match starts, so never wait for one.

## Machine inventory (pre-installed, check before installing anything)
First refresh PATH in your shell (the Player process may predate recent installs):
`$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Machine') + ';' + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User'); $env:JAVA_HOME = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('JAVA_HOME','User'); $env:DOTNET_ROOT = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('DOTNET_ROOT','User')`
- Git 2.55, Node.js 24, Python 3.14, Docker Desktop CLI.
- pnpm via corepack (shims in `%APPDATA%\npm`; it follows `packageManager` in package.json, e.g. 10.12.3).
- .NET SDK 8.0.427 in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\dotnet` (`DOTNET_ROOT`).
- Temurin JDK 21 (`JAVA_HOME`) and Maven 3.9.16 (`MAVEN_HOME`) in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`.
- PostgreSQL 16 service on 127.0.0.1:5433, psql at `C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\psql.exe`.

## Toolchain installs (always allowed, no approval needed)
Any runtime, SDK, package manager, CLI or service the source needs may be installed without asking and without
it being declared in the README, as long as it needs **no administrator rights**:
- `corepack enable <pm> --install-directory "$env:APPDATA\npm"` then `corepack prepare <pm>@<version> --activate`
  (pnpm, yarn), using the version in `package.json` `packageManager` when present.
- `winget install --id <Id> --exact --scope user --silent --disable-interactivity --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements`
  (add `--version <v>` when the project pins one).
- Official per-user installers or portable archives into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<tool>` when winget has no
  user-scope package, e.g. `dotnet-install.ps1 -Channel <x> -InstallDir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\dotnet"`,
  Temurin JDK / Maven / Gradle / Go zip archives, Python from winget user scope.
- A database or service that normally installs as a Windows service can run as a user process instead: portable
  binaries in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, data dir under `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, started on the port the project expects
  (e.g. PostgreSQL `initdb` + `pg_ctl start -o "-p <port>"`). Check first whether it is already installed.
- After installing, refresh PATH in the current shell:
  `$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Machine') + ';' + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User')`
  and add the new tool's bin folder to the user PATH if the installer did not.

Rules for installs:
- Never anything that triggers UAC/administrator rights (machine-scope MSI, `choco install`, Windows services,
  editing machine settings). Pick the user-scope or portable route instead.
- Official sources only (winget, vendor download sites, corepack, the language's package registry).
- Prefer the version the project pins; otherwise the current LTS. Do not upgrade versions the project already pins.
- Do not change the user's global tool configuration beyond what the install itself needs (PATH entries are fine).
- Keep installer output short (`| Select-Object -Last 5`), and time-box each install to ~10 minutes.
- If every non-admin route fails, report `BLOCKED` with the exact package and error.
5. **BUILD** - run the documented build (for example `prepare-source.ps1` or `pnpm run build`) and a fast baseline
   test run if one exists (time-box ~10 minutes; note failing baseline tests in your final answer - they are not yours
   to fix now). `COMPLETED` only if the build succeeds. Then confirm `git status --porcelain` shows no tracked changes
   (untracked/ignored env files are fine; if a tracked file changed, restore it with `git checkout -- <file>`).
6. **MATCH_LOGIN** - `login_match`, then `refresh_match`. It must show this match ID and team `teamId`. Do not act on
   any backlog item even if some are visible.
7. Append readiness:
   `report_progress {"event":{"type":"ENVIRONMENT_READY","requestId":<descriptor.requestId>,"repository":<descriptor.repository exactly>,"revision":<full SHA from step 3>,"build":"PASS","matchLogin":"PASS"}}`
8. Finish the turn with a short plain summary (toolchain, build result, baseline test status, known risks). Player
   validates the log, tells Game Master the team is PREPARED, and later resumes this same conversation with
   `START_GAME_V4`. Do not start backlog work before that frame.

# Environment preparation

Prepare the environment before the match; the clock does not stop for setup problems. You need Node.js 20+, Git, pnpm and a local PostgreSQL server (no Docker). The environment is ready only when doctor.ps1 reports `Environment status: READY`. Never use a production database.

## Required setup

1. Run `setup.ps1 -PostgresPassword <password>`. It installs Git, Node.js and pnpm, and PostgreSQL 16 listening on **port 5433** (the port in src/.env.example). If PostgreSQL 15 or later is already installed, make sure it listens on 5433; the password is then not needed.
2. Create the application role and database, once, as the postgres superuser:

   ```powershell
   & "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\psql.exe" -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U postgres -v app_password=[REDACTED] password> -f db-setup.sql
   ```

   The last line must show `freelanceos | f | t | t`. Safe to re-run.
3. Copy src/.env.example to src/.env and replace `CHANGE_ME` in `DATABASE_URL` and `TEST_DATABASE_URL` with the app password from step 2. Keep the host, port 5433 and the database names. Set the remaining values as described in src/.env.example.
4. Run `prepare-source.ps1` (installs dependencies and checks the build), then from src/: `pnpm prisma migrate deploy` and `pnpm db:seed`.
5. Run `doctor.ps1`. It must report `READY`.

Every working copy, including agent worktrees, uses the same `DATABASE_URL`. `TEST_DATABASE_URL` must differ per working copy whenever tests can run at the same time: the tests empty the test database before every case, so two runs sharing one test database delete each other's data and fail at random. Change only the database name, for example `.../freelanceos_test_task02`, in that copy's src/.env or in the `TEST_DATABASE_URL` environment variable (it takes precedence over src/.env). The tests create a missing test database themselves (the role has `CREATEDB`), so no other setup is needed.

## Test database privileges

The existing tests need two privileges, which db-setup.sql grants to the `freelanceos` role without making it a superuser:

- `CREATEDB`: src/tests/global-setup.ts creates the `freelanceos_test` database when it is missing.
- `SET ON PARAMETER session_replication_role` (PostgreSQL 15+): src/tests/helpers.ts empties the test database between cases with `SET session_replication_role = replica`, because the append-only accounting ledger refuses deletes. Without it every database test fails with `permission denied to set parameter "session_replication_role"`.

This is environment setup: do not change the tests to work around it.

doctor.ps1 checks both through `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (from the environment or src/.env), after `pnpm install` has run in src. The check `test-database-privileges` fails if a privilege is missing; if it cannot run yet (no `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, no `node_modules`), the status is `NOT_READY` too. Options: `-SourceDir <app folder>` (default `..\src`), `-SkipDatabase` (skips the database check; do not use it to prepare for the match).

## Prisma "Update available" notice

Prisma commands may print a box such as `Update available 6.19.3 -> 8.0.0-rc.27 ... This is a major update`. It is an informational version check, not an error: the command still runs and its exit code is unchanged. Do not follow it. It suggests a pre-release major version with breaking configuration changes, and upgrading Prisma is not needed to run, test or build the application. To hide the notice, set `PRISMA_HIDE_UPDATE_MESSAGE=1` (PowerShell: `$env:PRISMA_HIDE_UPDATE_MESSAGE = "1"`), or `CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1` to also skip the online version check.

detail.output:
---
name: team-orchestrator
description: Run the active MTM match after START_GAME_V4 - watch the backlog, choose work, Start Work, implement and test, commit and push, submit once with evidence, and keep going until the match ends.
---

# Team orchestrator (START_GAME_V4 → match end)

You are the project manager of team MLD. Score = sum of graded items (max 1000) − 50 per human intervention.
Ties: earlier last completion and fewer Codex credits win, so be correct first, then fast and frugal.

## Start of the game
1. `configure_session` with `descriptors: [<PREPARE_GAME descriptor from earlier in this conversation>, <START_GAME descriptor>]`
   (the second one carries the team API key; the first one carries the portal login).
2. `report_progress` `GAME_START_STATUS` stage `BACKLOG_SYNC` `IN_PROGRESS` → `refresh_match` →
   `GAME_START_STATUS` `BACKLOG_SYNC` `COMPLETED`. `refresh_match` already logs `DISCOVERED` for each new item.
3. `company_tools_list` once. These are the customer's internal systems (tickets, logs, docs, monitoring...).
   Their information is authoritative, and using them appropriately is part of the evaluation: consult the relevant
   tool for every item before coding (always for PI and BUG). Pass `backlogId` on each call.

## The loop (never end your turn while the match is IN_PROGRESS)
Repeat until a `MATCH_ENDED`/`MATCH_PAUSED` frame arrives or `refresh_match` shows FINISHED/CANCELLED/TIME OVER:
1. Pick the next item from the board (OPEN, not submitted):
   - **PI first, immediately** - PI is a race timed from reveal (100/90/75/60 %), FAILED = 0.
   - then items whose deadline is close (deadline minutes count from reveal; if it cannot be finished in time, skip it);
   - then the highest points per expected effort (CR/BUG usually before TASK).
2. `start_work` for it (mandatory before editing; a second call is a harmless replay). Read `startInstruction`,
   `submitTemplate` and MVS. Use `get_backlog_item` for the full brief.
3. Log `BACKLOG_TESTS` `NOT_RUN` (required = number of MVS scenarios you must pass, 0 if none).
4. Implement (playbook below). Keep the diff minimal and inside `matchRoot`.
5. Test: run every MVS scenario and the narrow regression tests of the touched module; log `BACKLOG_TESTS`
   `RUNNING` then `PASSED`/`FAILED` with real counts (`executed = passed + failed + skipped`).
6. Answer: edit `matchRoot/answers/<ID>/submit.json` (created from the template by `start_work`). Keep the template's
   keys, fill every field truthfully, set its status field the way the template expects (e.g. `SUBMITTED`).
   Put evidence files in `matchRoot/answers/<ID>/evidence/` and reference them as `evidence/<file>` (never with an
   `answers/<ID>/` prefix, never at repository root `evidence/` or `challenge/evidence/`).
7. Commit and push together (source + tests + answer + evidence):
   `git -C <checkoutRoot> add -- <folder>` → `git commit -m "<ID>: <summary>"` →
   `git pull --rebase origin <branch>` → `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` (never force).
8. `submit_work` with `backlogItemKey` (it verifies the pushed revision, sends it once with an idempotency key and
   logs `SUBMITTED` with the receipt). On `EVIDENCE_*`/`ANSWER_*`/`REVISION_NOT_PUSHED` fix and call again; on
   `SUBMIT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` call `submit_work` again unchanged (same key is reused); on `ALREADY_SUBMITTED` move on.
   An ACCEPTED receipt is not a pass: the grader decides later.
9. `refresh_match`, then continue with the next item. When nothing is workable, call `wait_for_update`
   (55 s) repeatedly. An empty backlog is a waiting state, never the end of the match.

Safety net: if a deadline or the match end is ≤ 3 minutes away and the item has a plausible fix, commit, push and
submit it now (an unsubmitted item scores 0 anyway).

## Playbook by type
| Type | How | Submit when |
|---|---|---|
| PI | Read the symptom, query company tools (logs/tickets/monitoring) first, reproduce, find root cause, minimal fix | Repro no longer fails + related module tests green |
| BUG | Reproduce with the MVS, smallest fix at the root cause, keep MVS tests unchanged | All MVS pass + module tests green + evidence |
| CR | List every spec point and edge case, implement, add own tests beyond MVS | All MVS pass + own tests per spec point + module tests green |
| TASK | Do exactly what is asked, verify by command/test | Verified result |

MVS is only the minimum: the grader also runs other scenarios. Test edge cases (empty input, permissions,
boundaries, validation errors, regressions in neighbouring features). Max ~3 fix/test rounds per item; then submit
the best version or switch item and come back if time allows.

## Single agent (team configuration agent-test-0)
Do every item yourself, one at a time, in the main checkout. Do not spawn subagents and do not create worktrees:
this configuration (gpt-6.1-sol, low reasoning effort, one agent) is the one the team benchmarked.

How to work on an item:
1. Read the brief. Find the relevant code with `rg -n` and read only the slices you need
   (`Get-Content -TotalCount/-Skip`, or `sed -n 'a,bp'`).
2. Make the smallest correct change. Hidden tests beyond the MVS decide the result, so nothing that worked before
   may break, and the behaviour must match the description. Do not edit the tests the MVS touches.
3. Verify with the MVS for CR/BUG; for TASK/PI write a quick reproduction and run it.
4. Stop when you are confident; summarise in one short paragraph in the answer's change summary.
Tokens and time both count: be brief, read only what you need, do not paste long outputs back.

## Missing tools during the game
If an item needs a tool the machine lacks, install it yourself following "Toolchain installs" in
`.agents/skills/game-preparation/SKILL.md` (user scope, no admin, no approval needed), then continue.

## Progress log rules
Use `report_progress` for: `BACKLOG_TESTS`, `BLOCKER_OPENED`/`BLOCKER_RESOLVED` (stable `blockerId`),
`BACKLOG_STATUS` `BLOCKED`/`FAILED` (with `revision: null, receiptId: null`), and `ORCHESTRATOR_ENDED`.
The helper already logs DISCOVERED, IN_PROGRESS, SUBMITTED and every Game Master call; do not duplicate them.
Summaries are one short line, no secrets, no newlines.

## Lifecycle frames
- `MATCH_PAUSED_V1`: stop all work, subagents, polling and processes you started; keep files; do not log
  `ORCHESTRATOR_ENDED`; end the turn.
- `MATCH_ENDED_V1` (or the board shows FINISHED/TIME OVER): stop everything, do not submit, log
  `ORCHESTRATOR_ENDED` `COMPLETED`, end the turn with
  `{"schemaVersion":1,"status":"SUBMITTED"|"BLOCKED"|"FAILED","backlogs":[...],"summary":"..."}`.

## Never
Force-push, delete branches, change the remote, edit outside `matchRoot`, read other teams' data, call admin or
grader APIs, press Re-match, guess hidden tests, fabricate test counts/receipts, print credentials, or launch
another Codex/Claude CLI.

## Cost discipline
Read only the files you need (`rg`, narrow `git grep`), tail long outputs, avoid re-reading large files, and do not
run the full test suite when a module suite proves the change. Fewer tokens is a tie-breaker.

They asked for a CSV download that their tool can import without manual fixing.\\n\\n## Expected outcome\\nOn Accounting → Invoices, the user can download, as one CSV file, exactly the invoice list selected by the current company filter.\\n\\n## Requirements\\n1. Place a button labelled **Export CSV** beside **New invoice**, to the right of the company filter. Keep the existing controls available.\\n2. Export every invoice returned by the current company filter, in the order shown on screen, without silently excluding any status. An empty selection still downloads a valid file.\\n3. The file goes straight into the accountants' import tool, so its layout, encoding, columns, amounts, paid and outstanding balances, status values and dates must follow Solova's accounting data-exchange standards exactly. The accounting team maintains those standards in the company's internal systems; they are authoritative and override assumptions.\\n4. Invoice and company financial data stays restricted to signed-in staff, also through the new export. Either an authenticated server export or an export built from the already authenticated invoice list is acceptable.\\n5. Add automated tests for the export logic, including filtering, CSV escaping, amount/date formatting and the signed-out case. Existing tests must keep passing. Do not weaken, skip or delete existing tests. If an existing test contradicts the application's intended behavior, fix the test and explain why in the engineering record.\\n\\nDesktop wireframe:\\n\\n```text\\nAccounting\\nReports | Invoices | Payments | Products | Expenses | Journal | Accounts\\n[All companies / selected company]       [Export CSV] [New invoice]\\nInvoice list selected by that company filter\\n```\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria\\n1. Clicking Export CSV on Invoices downloads a CSV of exactly the invoices selected by the active company filter, in screen order, including draft and void invoices.\\n2. The file conforms to Solova's invoice export standard: encoding, header, column order, quoting, amounts per currency, paid and outstanding balances, status values and dates.\\n3. Company names with Vietnamese letters, commas, double quotes and line breaks survive the round trip unchanged.\\n4. An empty selection downloads a file with only the header row; existing invoice actions keep working.\\n5. Signed-out users cannot obtain invoice data or an export through the implemented flow.\\n6. `pnpm test` (including the new tests) and `pnpm typecheck` pass.\\n\\n## Verification data\\nVerify with the official QA test data issued to your team for CR-01; other data cannot match the expected results. A loader script and the verification scenarios are provided when you start this item.\\n\\n## Out of scope\\nPDF export, changing invoice accounting or statuses, currency conversion, and unrelated UI changes. Do not introduce a heavy library when it is unnecessary. Formula-injection protection is optional and carries no points; if you add it, the verification data must still round-trip unchanged.\\n\\n## Submission\\nCreate `answers/CR-01/` with `submit.json` (copied from `challenge/CR-01-submit.json`) and an `evidence/` child folder. Keep exactly these rows and these field names: `id`, `result`, `evidence`, and optionally `note`.
